hero.subtitle: Serial/USB or Wi-Fi connection, buffer-safe G-code streaming, vector editor, image import, QR/barcode, materials, production queue, and 11 themes — all in one native, free, open-source (MIT) app.
hero.note: No account. No cloud. No subscription. Your files stay on your machine.

compat.label: Compatible with
compat.note: Ready profiles for 30+ models. Brands mentioned only to indicate compatibility.

porque.description: LaserGRBL is a Windows reference, but on Linux it depends on compatibility layers. GRBL Studio was born native: install, open, and talk to your machine without mapping COM ports or fighting the system.

cards.title: Really connects
cards.desc: USB serial or Wi-Fi/TCP with ESP8266/ESP32. The app reads firmware, work area, and limits and uses them in pre-flight.

cards.title: Respects the buffer
cards.desc: Character-counted send window (bytes), not lines. Each ok frees space — no bulk writes that lock the machine.

cards.title: Everything in one place
cards.desc: From idea to finished part without leaving the app. Vector, image, QR, barcode, materials, preview, simulation, production.

bad.title: LaserGRBL on Linux
bad.desc: Wine + Mono + COM port mapping. Works, but not native.

good.title: GRBL Studio
good.desc: AppImage + /dev/ttyUSB0 + native theme. Opened, connected, engraved.

cards.title: Reliable engraving
cards.desc: Floating bar with progress, feed/velocity/power overrides, pause/resume, emergency button — all with single-byte real-time commands.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio floating engraving bar with progress, pause, overrides, and emergency button.

cards.title: Vector editor
cards.desc: Millimeter canvas, shapes, layers, booleans, offset, kerf, nesting, SVG/DXF/PDF export. Draw or import and edit right in the app.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio vector editor with millimeter canvas, shapes, layers, and properties.

cards.title: Image → G-code
cards.desc: Line-to-line, dithering (Floyd–Steinberg, Atkinson, Bayer), centerline (skel), vectorization (potrace). Contrast, gamma, invert, rotate adjustments.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio image import tab with adjustments and engraving preview.

cards.title: QR Code & Data Matrix
cards.desc: QR Code (Micro QR), Data Matrix, PDF417, Aztec. Size, error correction, quiet zone, HRI. Generates vector or raster straight to G-code.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio QR Code generator with size, error correction, and quiet zone.
cards.imgAlt2: GRBL Studio Code 128 barcode generator with HRI and millimeter dimensions.

cards.title: Batch production
cards.desc: Persistent queue, N× copies mode, pause between pieces, counter, resume after failure, execution log. Designed for repeatability at the bench.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio production mode with copy counter and inter-piece pause.

cards.title: Materials catalog
cards.desc: Sheets with J/mm² dose, speed, power, passes, kerf, safety warnings, material test, focus test. Create and share your presets.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio materials catalog with sheets, recommendations, and safety warnings.

cards.title: 2D preview & simulation
cards.desc: Engraving path colored by layer/operation, animated progress, time simulation, machine limits, smooth zoom/pan.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio 2D preview with engraving path, progress, and simulation.

cards.title: 11 themes & 3 languages
cards.desc: Dark (default), light, high contrast, solarized, dracula, nord, one dark, github, monokai, gruvbox, tokyo night. UI in PT, EN, ES.
cards.imgAlt: GRBL Studio appearance screen with 11 themes and Portuguese, English, Spanish languages.

steps.title: Connect
steps.desc: Plug in via USB or configure Wi-Fi/TCP. The app detects firmware, reads limits and work area, and validates the connection.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.desc: Open G-code, import image, draw vector, or generate QR/barcode. Apply offset, kerf, nesting, organize in layers.

steps.title: Pre-flight
steps.desc: Automatic validation: machine area, laser power/mode, dangerous lines, unsupported commands. Fix before engraving.

steps.title: Engrave
steps.desc: Send with byte-counted window, monitor real-time DRO, use overrides, pause/resume, emergency stop. N× queue for production.

preflight.title: Pre-flight: validation before engraving
preflight.imgAlt: GRBL Studio pre-flight with limits, power, and dangerous lines validation.

appimage.title: AppImage (recommended)

appimage.note: Requires FUSE 2 (libfuse2) installed — present on most distros.

faq.description: Straight answers to the most common questions. If yours isn't here, open an issue on

questions.a: Yes. GRBL Studio is open source under MIT license, no subscription, account, or cloud. You download, use, and contribute if you want.

questions.q: Does it work with my GRBL laser?
questions.a: If the machine speaks GRBL 1.1 or 0.9, yes. USB serial and Wi-Fi/TCP for ESP8266/ESP32, plus 30+ ready profiles and a Generic GRBL profile.

questions.q: Do I need Wine or Mono?
questions.a: No. GRBL Studio is a native Linux desktop app, distributed as AppImage and .deb. Flatpak is in preparation.
G-code (.gcode, .nc, .tap, .txt), images PNG, JPG, BMP, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG, DXF ASCII, vector PDF. You can also draw in the internal editor.

For GRBL diode lasers, GRBL Studio covers the main flow: connection, preview, image, vector, layers, materials, production. No camera, rotary, or CO2/Ruida controllers; if you need those, LightBurn is still the choice.

questions.q: How do I install on Linux?
questions.a: Download the AppImage and run, or install the .deb. For serial port access, add your user to the dialout group and logout/login.

questions.q: Is there a manual in English?
questions.a: Yes. The full manual is available in Portuguese, English, and Spanish, with localized screenshots and browsable HTML.

questions.q: Where do I report bugs or request features?
questions.a: On the project's GitHub Issues. Code is open and contributions welcome.
